name: Wireframing Studio
description: A human-driven workspace for creating, editing, linking, auditing, and exporting production-grade application wireframe flows.
readme:
# Wireframing Studio

A production-grade, human-driven wireframing tool for the Lean AI Factory. It's the
**editable-flow surface** the `libraries/mcp/wireframing` README promises — a person places
elements, links screens, and adjusts the flow, with a **live A–F flow grade** that mirrors the
factory's automated audit.

Zero dependencies, no build step, no server. It's a single self-contained `index.html`.

## Run

Just open it:

```bash
# Windows
start index.html
# macOS
open index.html
# or double-click index.html in a file browser
```

(Optional) serve it if your browser restricts `file://`:

```bash
python -m http.server 8000   # then visit http://localhost:8000/libraries/code/wireframe-studio/
```

Everything autosaves to the browser's `localStorage`. Use **Import / Export** to move a design
between machines or into the pipeline.

### If it ever loads blank

The app self-heals: if a saved state fails to render, it automatically discards it and loads a
clean project. If you're on an older cached copy, **hard-refresh** (`Ctrl+Shift+R`) to pick up
the latest, or click **Reset & reload** on the error banner. **New** (top bar) always gives you a
blank project. Rendering is section-isolated and wrapped in a global error handler, so a single
failure can never freeze the whole tool.

## What it does

- **Canvas of screens** — drag to arrange, pan (drag empty space), zoom (Ctrl/⌘+scroll or the zoom bar), **Fit** to frame all.
- **iOS-aware component palette** — nav bar, tab bar, title, text, button, list link, list, text field, search, toggle, image, card. Click to add to the selected screen.
- **Inspector** — edit labels, placeholders, list rows, back button, tab bars; mark a button's **Action**; set an element's **link → target screen** (or "Draw link on canvas" then click the target).
- **Live flow audit** (right panel) — recomputed on every edit, showing the grade, the exact failing issues, and metrics.
- **Undo/redo** (Ctrl/⌘+Z · Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z), **Delete** to remove the selection, **Esc** to cancel linking.

## Flow audit — same rules as the factory

The live grade uses the **same thresholds** as `agents/wireframing/src/wireframing/audit.py`:

| Rule | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Clicks to a key action | ≤ 3 |
| Interactive features per screen | ≤ 7 |
| Max navigation depth | ≤ 4 |
| Orphan screens (unreachable) | 0 |
| Dead links (target missing) | 0 |

Grade `A` = none of the above violated **and** at least one primary Action is defined.
Each additional issue drops the grade `A → B → C → D → F`, matching the Python audit exactly.

> A link is only a link when you draw it. That's what kills the classic hallucinated-flow
> failure mode (buttons to nowhere, unlinked pages) — you can't create a dead end by accident,
> and the audit flags any you do create.

## Exports

| Export | File | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Studio spec** | `*.studio.json` | Full-fidelity, re-importable (canvas positions + components). |
| **Factory WireframeSpec** | `*.wireframe.json` | Directly consumable by `wireframing/generate.py` + `audit.py`. Shape matches `WireframeSpec` (screens → `id, title, elements[], links[], actions[]`). The start screen is emitted as `index` so the factory auditor's default entry (`index.html`) grades from the correct screen. Verified: export → `generate.py` → `audit.py` returns **grade A**. |
| **Interactive prototype** | `*.prototype.html` | Self-contained clickable phone prototype — share it, click through the real flow. |
| **SwiftUI scaffold** | `*.swift` | Structural handoff for Sprint Engineers: a `NavigationStack` + one `View` per screen, `NavigationLink`s for drawn links. |
| **Wireframe image** | `*.svg` / `*.png` | Flat snapshot of the flow for docs/retros. |

Import accepts either a **Studio spec** or a plain **factory WireframeSpec** (it rebuilds an
editable model from the latter), so it round-trips with the existing `agents/wireframing`
output.

## How it fits the factory

```
charter ─▶ WireframingAgent (LLM draft) ─▶ *.wireframe.json ─┐
                                                             ├─▶ Wireframing Studio (human adjusts)
prior work / from scratch ───────────────────────────────────┘        │
                                                                        ├─▶ *.wireframe.json ─▶ generate.py / audit.py
                                                                        ├─▶ *.prototype.html (review the flow)
                                                                        └─▶ *.swift (SwiftUI handoff)
```

The agent can draft a flow headlessly; a human opens the Studio to adjust it (add a button →
target, rename, add content) exactly as the MCP README describes; the "A"-grade result flows
back into the sprint gate chain (ux-audit → compliance → security) unchanged.

## Data model

Compatible superset of `WireframeSpec`. A screen carries canvas position + typed components:

```jsonc
{
  "meta": { "name": "My App", "entry": "home" },
  "screens": [
    {
      "id": "home", "title": "Home", "x": 60, "y": 60,
      "comps": [
        { "id": "c1", "kind": "navbar", "label": "My App", "props": {} },
        { "id": "c2", "kind": "button", "label": "Get started",
          "props": {}, "action": "start", "linkTo": "onboard" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`toFactorySpec()` projects this down to the exact `{screens:[{id,title,elements,links,actions}]}`
the Python generator/auditor expect — no logic is duplicated; the JS audit intentionally
mirrors `audit.py`'s thresholds so both tools agree on a grade.

## Tests

The core logic (audit grading, factory projection, exports) is validated headlessly with a
small Node + DOM-shim harness — grade-A sample, dead-link/orphan/over-feature detection,
prototype/SwiftUI generation, and a factory export→import→re-audit round trip. See the commit
notes; the tool itself needs no runtime.
